rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Pickomino 1.1 Introduction 1.2 Objective 1.3 Game Play 1.4 End of Turn Actions 1.5 End of Game 1.6 Hints Pickomino Introduction Pickomino is a dice drafting and tile collecting game with "push your luck" elements. The BGA game is based on the 40th anniversary edition, in which players are meerkats competing to gather tasty bugs. Objective The goal of the game is to gather more bugs than your opponents. You do this by using a combination of dice rolls to either win tiles from the playing area or steal tiles from other players. Game Play 1. Roll the dice. Choose one die face. All the dice matching that die face are moved and put into the "collection line" below the game board. For example, if you rolled some 3s, you could choose them and they would all be added to the collection line. 2. Once you've added dice to the collection line, you can choose to re-roll the remaining dice. However, you cannot choose any dice fave/value that is already in the collection line. For example, you might roll a 5 and decide to add it to the collection line. If you choose to re-roll the remaining dice and get additional 5s, you will not be allowed to choose them. 3. Your score so far is shown on the right hand side of the collection line. This is calculated as a total of all the dice pips, plus 5 points for each "paw print" die face. 4. To win a tile, you must have at least 1 paw print in your line by the end of the turn. 5. Continue re-rolling dice until either: - You are happy with your current score, or - There are no more dice to roll, or - You can't add any more dice to your line, in which case you BUST You can now do the end of turn actions. End of Turn Actions If you have busted, not scored enough to collect a tile, or you do not have a paw print, you will not be able to collect a tile. In this case, you lose the top-most tile from your hand, which is returned to the centre, and the highest-value tile in the middle is flipped face-down, removing it from play. (If you don't have any tiles, there is no penalty and no tile is flipped.) If you have a paw print in your line, you may now choose a tile from those available: - If a tile (whether in the centre or on the top of another player's stack) exactly matches the sum of your dice in the collection line you must take it. - Otherwise, you may take any tile that is worth less than your score from the playing area. Your new tile is placed on top of any existing tiles you have already collected. This protects the existing tiles, as your opponents can only steal the top-most tile. Play now passes clockwise to the next player. End of Game The game ends when there are no more tiles available in the centre. Final scores are calculated by the number of bugs shown on each tile (not the tile value). The player with the most bugs is the winner. If there is a tie, the player with the highest numbered tile in their possession is the winner. Hints - Remember that you need to add at least one paw print to your dice collection line, on each turn. - To get higher value tiles, you could hold out for more than one paw print to boost your score, but you run the risk of getting none. - Lower value tiles are easier to obtain, but are also easier for opponents to steal. - Remember that the final score is based on the number of bugs on the tile, not the value of the tiles.

---

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Yet another dice-rolling game, which seems to borrow from Can't Stop. What do people get from those?

[Rating: 1/10] The only thing you gotta do is roll dice. Tactics are low or unexisting. And the theme isn't particularly fun.

[Rating: 2/10] Concrete evidence that Yatzee and worms do not mix.  Playing at very brisk speeds, this game took way too long, and simply did not have the depth to sustain it.

[Rating: 2/10] I have no desire to play this again - what are those people who give this game a high rating smoking when they play it?

[Rating: 2/10] Random, push your luck dice game.  Even as a filler it fails, as the games can go on far longer than expected. It seems that overall the decisions are obvious.  Roll well and win, roll poorly and lose.  The downtime is obnoxious, but it is perfect for sitting on the toilet while waiting your turn.

[Rating: 2/10] I loathe dice games. If only it had a fixed number of rolls I'd know when it ends.

[Rating: 2/10] I tried to give it a chance and played it with different groups for maybe six times, but I never got over the strong feeling that it would probably be more fun to stick a fork in my stomach than to play this game.  EDIT: I recently went and bought Sushizock in Gockelwock which definately is a better game with similar mechanics and shorter playtime (though only good for two people).

[Rating: 2/10] Why play this, which is really quite boring, when you could play To Court The King, which is much less boring. Or Yahtzee, what ever happened to Yahtzee?

[Rating: 2/10] The goal is not to get the highest amount of worms, it's to be the only player to get worms. In a 7 player game, I think only 2-3 players ended up with 1 tile. The concept is interesting but the game is so hard because it's so easy to lose the tiles you have.
